A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DistFlow framework and provide readable text, diagrams, experimental plots, and references. Both contain Figures 1–14 and Table 1. Neither contains an appendix, and no material extraction gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original throughput, GPU scalability, long-context, and training-convergence experiments in Section 7.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports revised scalability measurements in Figure 11.

M1.justification: The DAG planner, worker execution, distributed loading, and shared-memory/all-to-all redistribution procedures remain unchanged. Megatron, newly mentioned in the overview, already appears among worker backends in v1 Section 5. Adding Actor Forward to Figure 1's background diagrams does not establish a change to DistFlow's proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate language-model training on DeepScaleR-Preview-Dataset and multimodal training on MM-Eureka-Dataset. The GPU-scaling, long-context, and convergence scenarios are retained without additional datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: verl v0.4.0 remains the sole evaluated comparator in the corresponding throughput, constrained-batch, long-context, and convergence experiments. Changes to citations do not introduce additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 7.1 retains the stated models, hardware, software, FSDP/vLLM backends, and length limits; convergence still uses 20 epochs and 700 steps. Equation 1 expresses the normalized per-GPU throughput retention already used in v1. Deleted batch-size disclosures do not establish that settings changed.

E4.justification: The same scaling, long-context, and convergence questions are investigated. No ablation, new robustness procedure, error analysis, or case study is added or removed. Figure 11 supplies revised measurements for an existing evaluation.

E5.justification: Both average throughput over several iterations after warm-up. Neither adds explicit repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figure 11 replaces all three scalability curves: for example, the plotted 72B throughput at 1024 GPUs changes from approximately 104k to 205k tokens/s. Section 7.3 changes the stated 32B efficiency from 80.5% to 93.9%, although v3's plotted 64-to-512-GPU endpoints imply approximately 90%. These substantially revise central results. Other performance plots and Table 1 retain their measurements. Missing batch sizes and an unexplained revision prevent treating the changes as established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Neither version presents theoretical propositions or proofs. v3's Equation 1 states the standard scaling-efficiency formula for the throughput-per-GPU retention already discussed in v1; it does not introduce new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows scalability from 'thousands of GPUs' to 1024 GPUs, and the abstract and contribution list explicitly qualify the 7x improvement as occurring in specific scenarios. The distributed architecture, DAG flexibility, and throughput contributions remain the same.

C2.justification: v3 removes the discussion attributing 72B scaling degradation beyond 256 GPUs to FSDP and proposing Megatron as a future remedy. It also more precisely attributes the centralized bottleneck to controller-managed data transfer and emphasizes independent optimization of control and data flow. Most performance interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 removes the model-dependent per-node batch sizes disclosed in the captions of Figures 9–11, without replacement elsewhere. Section 3 also drops instructions distinguishing required Model, Training, and Algorithm configurations from the optional DAG configuration. Most hardware, software, and backend details remain available.

R1.justification: Section 8 removes the Agent Frameworks for LLM Reasoning subsection and assertions that DistFlow improves reasoning capabilities and heterogeneous-hardware scaling or resilience. The background also drops its broader RL-scaling discussion. New citations include Attention Is All You Need, asynchronous deep RL, Pathways, and parameter servers. Together these substantially narrow and refocus the research positioning.

P1.justification: The background is extensively rewritten and reorganized, the system overview and data-coordination explanations are substantially compressed, and Section 8 loses an entire thematic subsection. Captions are systematically shortened. These are substantial editorial changes beyond renumbering; the author list also adds Yinhui Lu.

P2.justification: All 14 figures and Table 1 remain. Figure 1 adds Actor Forward nodes, Figure 3 corrects engine labels, and performance plots receive sizing, axis-label, or tick changes. Captions are shortened and Table 1 is relocated, while the overall two-column layout and display types remain stable.

improvement.justification: v3 improves focus, corrects the reference-model explanation, and narrows headline claims. However, it removes batch sizes needed to reproduce Figures 9–11 and the FSDP limitation discussion while substantially revising scalability results without explanation. Its new 93.9% efficiency statement is also not reconciled with Figure 11's approximately 90% endpoint-based value. These losses in reproducibility and numerical consistency modestly outweigh the editorial improvements.
